name: Riftcutter
description: Spirat raider turned outlaw legend—its serrated hull slices patrols like space sashimi, and every pirate swears they’ve seen it (they haven’t).

name: Riftcutter II
description: Spirat warship whispered about in starport cantinas—its serrated hull slices through patrol lines like prey, legendary among Dark Rift outlaws.

name: Korvaxia
description: Arch planet with toxic green seas—melts ships, melts flesh, and still somehow counts as prime real estate for archlords.

name: Drazkor
description: Acid-crater planet where Arch warbands prove themselves—basically space boot camp, but with more melting.

name: Akash Viridion
description: Webe parasite ship glowing sickly green—steals your systems, your energy, and your sense of personal space.

name: Akash
description: Webe vamp-ship with living circuits—sucks energy, ships, and probably your will to live straight into the hive.

name: Akash Husk
description: Webe dud-ship with glitchy circuits—glows orange, dies fast, and exists mainly so real ships don’t have to.

name: Aetheron
description: Cosmicon support craft that spams shields and heals—basically the cosmic intern keeping the fleet from falling apart.

name: Aetheron II
description: Cosmicon support ship that hands out shields and energy like cosmic candy—keeps fleets alive just long enough to regret their choices.

name: Aetheron III
description: Cosmicon support ship that babysits fleets with shields and heals—basically the cosmic cleric nobody admits they need.

name: Intersecta
description: Spirat beam ship that points a giant space-laser at you and refuses to blink—basically the galaxy’s worst staring contest.

name: Starfang
description: Spirat raider that looks like a star, fights like a wrecking ball—thrusters on max, brain cells on minimum.

name: Starfang II
description: Spirat raider shaped like a jagged star—bursts into convoys screaming 'subtlety is for other factions.'

name: Stinger
description: Spirat raider that looks like someone duct-taped a scrapyard to an engine—claws first, questions never.

name: Stinger II
description: Spirat raider covered in jagged claws—flies like a scrapyard nightmare and hugs convoys the way a bear hugs honey… violently.

name: Vega
description: Spirat raider that weaponized a trident-shaped prow—flies like lightning, hits like a thunder god with road rage.

name: Vega II
description: Spirat raider with a three-pronged prow—basically space’s deadliest fork, and it’s not here for salad.

name: Brainleech
description: Webe ship that slaps hulls with parasitic noodles—steals your power, your dignity, and maybe your Wi-Fi password.

name: Tigershark
description: Cosmicon strike ship with violet cores—cuts fleets with surgical beams, then growls about it like it’s doing you a favor.

name: Beluga
description: Webe void-whale wannabe—floats slow, looks harmless, then dumps hive energy like it’s allergic to subtlety.

name: Beluga II
description: Webe hive-ship shaped like a void-whale—drains fleets dry and looks ridiculous doing it. Space whaling, but grosser.

name: Dominator
description: Cosmicon support ship with all the firepower of a flashlight—its real job is being the galactic doorman for reinforcements.

name: Black Bird
description: Cosmicon heavy warship with glowing green guts—fires so much it looks less like strategy and more like a tantrum in space.

name: Black Bird II
description: Cosmicon warship that charges first and thinks never—basically heavy cannons strapped to bad decisions.

name: Black Bird III
description: Cosmicon bruiser that solves problems by dumping more firepower—subtlety not included in the design specs.

name: Ragnarok
description: Webe warship buzzing with bad wiring—technically 'common,' but still wrecks ships like it’s overcompensating for something.

name: Humpback Squad
description: Webe squad that lugs cargo and opens warp lanes—slow, ugly, and somehow still the reason the swarm shows up on time.

name: Crab
description: Cosmicon brawler with a crab shell hull—scuttles into battle, pinches formations, and somehow makes ramming look tactical.

name: Crab II
description: Cosmicon melee ship with a jagged shell—favorite pastime: headbutting fleets until something breaks (usually them).

name: Gridlock
description: Webe factory-fortress that cranks out swarms while turrets sweep the void—like an assembly line with trust issues.

name: Overclock
description: Webe spacestation made of angry circuits—spits out swarms faster than your GPU fan on a bad day.

name: Blitzer
description: Spirat melee ship with spiked prow—strategy is just 'ram harder' and pray the sparks count as style points.

name: Blitzer II
description: Spirat assault ship with electrified spikes—turns every head-on crash into a light show nobody asked for.

name: Blitzer III
description: Spirat ramming ship with more spikes than sense—its battle plan is basically 'hit forehead, repeat.'

name: Blitzer IV
description: Spirat strike ship with jagged prows—charges headfirst into fleets like it skipped pilot school on purpose.

name: Blitzer V
description: Spirat brawler that wins by headbutting ships—electrified prow, spiked hull, and zero concept of personal space.

name: Blitzer VI
description: Spirat raider with electrified spikes—flies straight into ships because aiming is overrated.

name: Spirat Emblem 2017
description: 2017 Skull badge of the Spirats—perfect for pirates who want their logo to scream 'yes, we bite.'

name: Cosmicrafts Emblem
description: The OG insignia—simple, angular, and basically the game’s baby photo that everyone still pretends looks cool.

name: League Emblem
description: Badge of Cosmicrafts ranked mode—flash it to show you’ve grinded more ladders than an interstellar janitor.

name: Neon Raider
description: Hand-painted relic from Cosmicrafts’ glow-up era—when 3D got ditched for 2D and style points actually mattered.

name: Wingflare
description: Webe light fighter with thrusters so bright they double as a rave—zips in, pokes holes, zips out before you blink.

name: Wingflare II
description: Webe light fighter that zips in neon streaks—great at hit-and-run strikes, terrible if it ever sticks around.

name: Wingflare III
description: Webe ship with thrusters so flashy it got promoted to company logo—proof that branding beats armor every time.

name: Ragnarok II
description: Webe heavy warship glowing red—shows up late, hits like the end of the world, and leaves nothing but cosmic ashes.

name: Dominator II
description: Cosmicon support ship with warp beacons—doesn’t hit hard, just calls in friends who do. Basically the galaxy’s ultimate plus-one.

name: Dominator III
description: Cosmicon support ship that drops allies into battle like an interstellar Uber—also famous for being the first ship NFT minted off ICP.

name: Double Pulverizer
description: Webe turret with two big guns—doesn’t move an inch, doesn’t need to, just turns anything dumb enough to get close into scrap confetti.

name: Dragonborn
description: Celestial ice planet that’s alive, cranky, and full of Spiral energy—basically a frozen parent that never stops whispering advice.

name: Dragonmaw Trio
description: Trio of Spirat siege ships that move slower than galactic tax forms—until they open their maws and turn fortresses into space gravel.

name: Dragonmaw Squad
description: Spirat siege pack that crawls forward like a lava parade—slow, ugly, and guaranteed to ruin your planet’s surface décor.

name: Dragonmaw
description: Epic Spirat warship that crawls forward like doom on thrusters—when its plasma breath hits, planets get heartburn.

name: Dragonmaw II
description: Spirat siege ship that lumbers forward spitting plasma—slow as a slug, but bites like a flamethrower dragon with indigestion.

name: Webe Emblem
description: Hex badge of the Webes—think space bees, but meaner, greener, and way less interested in honey.

name: Orion
description: Cosmicon fighter with sleek thrusters and sharp cannons—flies like a dream, breaks like a toy if you actually hit it.

name: Orion II
description: Cosmicon fighter that zips around with twin cannons—hits hard, dodges harder, and explodes if you sneeze on it.

name: Dulrissan
description: Celestial living planet that fires death beams—half homeworld, half cosmic rage monster. Bring sunscreen and extra fleets.

name: Dulrissan Arena
description: Celestial station where warriors duel, die, and get zapped back for round two—basically the galaxy’s most violent gym membership.

name: Pylon
description: Webe station that anchors warp lanes—stand near it and fleets appear out of nowhere, like really aggressive party crashers.

name: Energy Emblem
description: Golden lightning bolt badge—basically a giant 'low battery' warning, but way shinier.

name: Soul of Spacehawk
description: Early prototype soul from 2016—armored wings, big dreams, and the vibe of 'what if my doodle was the ultimate fighter?'

name: Starfighter
description: Cosmicon assault craft that trades agility for fire hose–levels of lasers. Subtle? No. Effective? Absolutely.

name: Dominator Squad
description: Cosmicon support squad that pins enemies with beams—great for teamwork, terrible if they all decide to aim at each other.

name: Starfighter II
description: Cosmicon assault ship with rapid-fire cannons—dogfights so long your trigger finger will need a vacation.

name: Soul of John Sorrow
description: Spirat legend in stickman mode—armed with a blaster, drawn like a 3rd grader’s homework. Legends gotta start somewhere.

name: Equinox
description: Cosmicon assault craft said to be forged under twin suns—shield and spear in one package, and just flashy enough to make common pilots jealous.

name: Equinox II
description: Cosmicon assault craft built for balance—steady guns, steady shields, steady paycheck. Not flashy, just stubbornly hard to kill.

name: Equinox III
description: Rare Cosmicon assault craft with emerald conduits and plasma-charged cannons—hits harder in formation, because peer pressure works in space too.

name: Equinox IV
description: Cosmicon assault craft with twin cannons and a stable core—nothing flashy, just the dependable kind of ship that never calls in sick.

name: Equinox V
description: Cosmicon assault ship seen from the rear—thrusters blazing like it just skipped leg day but never skipped back day.

name: Cosmicon Emblem
description: Badge of the Cosmicons—phoenix logo, shiny plating, and just enough smug tech pride to blind a fleet commander.

name: Starfighter III
description: Cosmicon assault craft with rapid-fire cannons—because sometimes the answer really is 'more bullets, faster.'

name: Starfighter Squad
description: Cosmicon fighters in formation—think laser-shotgun mode. One ship is annoying, twelve is overkill (and that’s the point).

name: Xenopulse
description: Webe strike craft built in swarms—cheap, fast, and zappy. Think space termites with better aim and worse manners.

name: Hivebreaker
description: Webe warship that skips ranged combat and just headbutts fleets—because sometimes the best strategy is 'hit harder.'

name: Siegebreaker
description: Cosmicon tankship with guns the size of small moons—slow to move, but once it parks, goodbye defenses, hello space rubble.

name: Siegebreaker Aegis
description: White-armored Cosmicon tankship that screams 'shoot me first.' Packs cannons big enough to flatten fleets and egos alike.

name: Siegebreaker II
description: Cosmicon brawler with twin plasma cannons—moves like a slug, hits like a meteor. Perfect for when you want walls to stop existing.

name: Siegebreaker III
description: Cosmicon artillery ship with triple plasma cannons—built to turn bunkers into bonfires, one rear shot at a time.

name: Voltragh
description: Webe energy planet crackling with blue veins—half power plant, half death trap. Orbit too close and get fried like cosmic toast.

name: The Fiery Core
description: Spade lava world that belches fire and brimstone—perfect vacation spot if you’re a demon, terrible if you’re anything else.

name: Spiral Pool Emblem
description: Epic badge of the Spiral Token—because nothing says galactic war like a liquidity pool. Spin it, stake it, pray it doesn’t drain.

name: Replay Emblem
description: Badge that lets you relive every glorious battle... and every humiliating misclick. Eternal cycles of war, now with instant replay.

name: Angry Flies to Drazkor
description: Legendary artwork of five Spirat warships racing to Drazkor—homage to vanished Angry Fly artists. Green engines blazing, subtlety isn't in their flight plan.

name: Stingray
description: Webe strike ship that glides like a manta and zaps like a storm—blink and it’s gone, but your hull isn’t.

name: Graviton
description: Webe bruiser with a giant gravity plate—moves slower than paperwork, hits harder than a black hole on payday.

name: Emblem of the Crystal of Ethereum
description: Celestial badge carved from Ethereum crystal—shines so bright it could blind a star, or at least your enemies’ fashion sense.

name: MK-IV Ultra
description: Cosmicon fighter blazing with starlight cores—fast, radiant, and more than happy to turn enemy armor into solar flare confetti.

name: The Terraformer
description: Cosmicon base that reshapes worlds to Wegnar’s will—half citadel, half planet-sized garden tool.

name: XRT Sentinel
description: Cosmicon station that spots cloaked ships and zaps them with a beam—because hide-and-seek isn’t fun when only one side gets to hide.

name: Starfang III
description: Spirat raider with a star-shaped hull that bites harder than it looks—because nothing says terror like getting shanked by geometry.

name: Stinger III
description: Spirat raider with jagged claw-hulls that smash convoys apart—because sometimes subtle piracy just doesn’t cut it.

name: Vega III
description: Three-pronged Spirat raider that slams ships full speed and fries them on impact—because subtlety is overrated.

name: Intersecta II
description: Spirat beam ship that locks on and never lets go—like a bad song stuck in your head, except it melts your hull instead.

name: Swarmer
description: Angry Flies sharpshooter—fires precision bolts that drain speed and pride. It doesn’t just kill you, it makes you late to your own funeral.

name: Cyclops
description: Cosmicon warship with one giant eye-core—because two would be overkill. Fires beams so far you’ll see the light before you see the ship.

name: Devastator Maelstrom
description: Artwork of Cosmicon warships launched from the Terraformer, descending on Dragonborn in a storm of fire and conquest.

name: Webe Prototype
description: Early 3D concept of Webe ships, showing angular frames and unstable energy cores before their final designs emerged.

name: Starfighter IV
description: Cosmicon assault craft with reinforced hull and rapid-fire cannons, built to flood battlefields with relentless volleys.

name: Warp Portal
description: Webe ring that tears Spiral rifts, warping fleets in and out on command.

name: Dinobot
description: Webe brawler that charges like a prehistoric nightmare—fast, heavy, and built to flatten fleets with one bad headbutt.

name: Type I
description: Cosmicon light craft powered by concentric energy rings. Gathers and unleashes blasts from radiant core, darting across battlefields like a living accelerator.

name: Trex
description: A Webe short-range assault ship shaped like a void-born T-Rex—small reach, huge bite, and an appetite for fast, close kills before darting back into the swarm.

name: Warhawk
description: The Warhawk: a Cosmicon scorpion with pincers that snap ships in half and armor that laughs at strategy. When it charges, you don’t fight—you get flattened.

name: Neon Spire
description: Rare Webe station—half synth, half bug zapper. Leaks violet charge, fries fleets, and nobody agrees if it’s a factory or a rave hive.

name: Hive Bastion
description: A rare Webe spacestation buzzing with green current. No one’s sure if it’s a factory, a fortress, or just hive paranoia—either way, it bites.

name: Pulse Hive
description: A rare Webe spacestation sparking with toxic green light. Maybe it’s a power grid, maybe it’s a trap—either way, don’t park near it.

name: Voltspire
description: A rare Webe spacestation humming with violet arcs. It looks like a fortress, but feels more like a live wire waiting for someone dumb enough to touch it.

name: Neon Crypt
description: Rare Webe station—a rave stuffed in a tomb, pulsing pink static like it might open a wormhole or just fry your Wi-Fi.

name: Gemini
description: Celestial marvel—tiny, radiant, and damn near indestructible. Gemini shreds fleets with twin strikes, proving size is just a mortal excuse.

name: CR3-Terminator
description: Legendary Webe machine. No feelings, no mercy, no coffee breaks—just a kill switch wrapped in armor, deleting fleets like bad code.

name: Oasia
description: A neutral world of extremes—lush crater-lakes ringed by endless desert. Half spa retreat, half survival nightmare. Bring sunscreen *and* a machete.

name: Maw's Nest
description: Rare Neutral planet—crater-lakes sparkle like treasure, but it’s a mirage scam: no shade, no mercy, just heatstroke deluxe.

name: Doom
description: Cosmicon Titan-class ship the size of a small city. Built to soak damage like a galactic punching bag, it bellows ridiculous thruster groans and cannon roars.

name: Orion III
description: Cosmicon fighter with wings like a duck, bite like a railgun. Quacks in plasma, not feathers.

name: Swarmer II
description: Snipes from the shadows and latches onto your engines, bleeding speed till you’re crawling like space roadkill. Classic Angry Flies hospitality.

name: Swarmer Mk.II
description: Same parasite, fancier paint job. White hull, pink thrusters—nothing says 'deadly sniper' like dressing it up like a space ice cream truck.

name: Swarmer Pixel Relic
description: Legendary Angry Flies sniper reimagined in 16-bit glory. Still a soulless parasite, but now it drains fleets one pixel at a time. Retro pain, modern suffering.

name: Gutlord
description: Relic from Cosmicrafts 2018 vaults: the Spirat clan leader who made bad hygiene a war crime. Merciless, loud, always covered in blood. Legendary artwork.

name: Capsule Emblem
description: The badge for consumables—because nothing says ‘progress’ like popping mystery pills for XP boosts. A shiny emblem of your fleet’s snack addiction.

name: Warp Halo
description: Rare Cosmicon ring station—spins itself dizzy to tear portals. Elegant, reliable, and only creepy if you’re the one getting pulled in.

name: Predator Pack
description: Four long Cosmicon destroyers flying like synchronized murder-fish, blasting anything dumb enough to line up. Fast, mean, and basically a space blender squad.

name: Predator
description: Rare Spirat destroyer—bright red, yellow trim swagger. Nothing screams terror like showing up to war dressed as a cartoon hero.

name: Predator II
description: Spirat Predator with faint magenta glow—the 'ran out of time' edition. Looks like someone left it half-finished in Photoshop and still called it battle-ready.

name: Predator III
description: Rare Spirat destroyer—white hull, purple trim, cyan glow. A front-facing rave shark here to steal your Wi-Fi and maybe your lunch.

name: Predator IV
description: Predator from the bottom—yes, we’re staring at its space belly. Not intimidating, just feels like it’s about to ask for tummy rubs before charging a cruiser.

name: Type I II
description: Rare Type I sporting MSGDI red-and-yellow skin—basically the hotrod edition of Cosmicon light craft. Same concentric ring pew-pew, now with extra style points.

name: Pulverizer
description: Rare Cosmicon turret-station—one oversized cannon. The bargain-bin Double Pulverizer, still blasting holes with half the overcompensation.

name: Podcrasher
description: Webe death-machine that went straight for ‘slam into it until it dies.’ A rare Webe ship that thinks speed = strategy. Pure kamikaze bot energy.

name: Ragnarok III
description: Upgraded Webe warship that hums like a broken fridge before it rips cruisers apart. Basically the soundtrack of your last mistake in space.

name: Ragnarok IV
description: Webe warship juiced up like it stole a neon rave. Twin plasma rings, blinding lights, and zero chill—basically a flying migraine coming straight at you.

name: Ragnarok V
description: Rare Spirat destroyer—blue, red, star slapped on. Cosplays freedom, fights like a drunk drone smashing into anything in range.

name: Ragnarok VI
description: Spirat warship with lilac paint job and radioactive green LEDs—a cosmic rave toy that forgot it's supposed to kill things, not host a dance floor.

name: Podcrasher II
description: Rare Webe interceptor—engines backwards, charges in reverse. A kamikaze pod proving 'death from behind' wasn’t meant this literal.

name: Podcrasher III
description: Pink-hulled Webe kamikaze pod with thrusters pointing the wrong way. Deadly in reverse, fabulous in color—because nothing says equality like exploding in style.

name: Infernode
description: Epic Spade planet—molten wannabe star, too hot for life, too dumb for fusion. A bitter rock we call a world before it explodes out of spite.

name: Trex II
description: Epic Webe destroyer—tiny arms, big bite. Basically a T. rex fossil strapped to afterburners, Jurassic Park reimagined as road rage.

name: Dinobot II
description: Webe assault ship shaped like a discount space dinosaur. Charges headfirst into fleets like it just escaped a prehistoric theme park with anger issues.

name: Trex III
description: Webe warship shaped like a tired T. rex—dark gray hull, head drooped like it’s over the cosmic grind. Less ‘roar’ and more ‘I need a nap.’

name: Harbinger
description: Legendary Celestial art—pipes glued to a fish, sold as divine. Survived 200 paint-overs, not for design but sheer stubbornness.

name: EGO
description: Webe's interplanetary defense base—'that one boss fight that ruins your weekend.' A giant floating middle finger to anyone dumb enough to invade Webe space.

name: Riftcutter Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet edition of the Spirat raider—same jagged murder-boat energy, now flattened into 2D frames so you can watch it slice space like an angry flipbook.

name: Akash Spritesheet
description: Common Spirat vamp-ship—drains fleets dry, now in pixel poses. Flip fast and it’s less terror, more hive laughing at flipbook carnage.

name: Aetheron Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Cosmicon space-cleric—every frame is just more shield spam and heal spam. Flip it fast and watch your fleet's HR intern try to matter.

name: Stinger Spritesheet
description: Common Spirat raider—junkyard stapled to a thruster. Pixel angles let you admire every bolt holding this space deathtrap together.

name: Starfang Spritesheet
description: Common Spirat raider—jagged star with zero subtlety. Each pixel frame is basically a neon sign flashing 'robbery in progress.'

name: Swarmer Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Spirat sniper leech—you can enjoy frame-by-frame misery as it drains your engines and crawls you into oblivion. Looks even slimier in motion.

name: Intersecta Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Spirat beam ship—frame after frame of one long, awkward space-laser stare. Blink and you lose, except it never does.

name: Vega Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Spirat trident-nosed raider—lightning with anger issues, broken into frames so you can relive every thunderous crash in slow motion.

name: Brainleech Spritesheet
description: Common Celestial parasite—tentacle slapstick in pixel form. A flipbook of your dignity getting siphoned away, frame by awkward frame.

name: Monolith Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe death-station—gravity drags ships in like a cosmic scam, then fries them with radiation. Frame by frame proof that physics hates you.

name: Barracuda Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon flagship—circular hull spitting glowing orbs like cosmic hairballs. Overkill framed in pixel perfection, shot by shot.

name: Drillshot
description: Webe basic unit with two gun barrels—nothing fancy, just a hive grunt spraying lead like it’s being paid in bullets. The cosmic definition of disposable.

name: Beluga Spritesheet
description: Common Celestial void-whale knockoff—drifts like space furniture, then spews hive energy on fleets. Majestic in the absolute worst way.

name: Humpback Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe humpback hauler—slow, fat, radiating pure 'space semi-truck' energy. Every frame is just interstellar traffic backed up by this unit.

name: Wolfhound Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon juggernaut—colossal artillery overcompensating hard. Pixel frames screaming 'don’t get within a lightyear' or else.

name: Blitzer Spritesheet
description: Common Spirat spike-rammer—every pixel frame is a self-zapping light show. Electrocutes itself and foes with pure space mosh pit energy.

name: Wingflare Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe showboat fighter—thrusters so blinding they double as marketing. Frame by frame proof that hive design is 90% glow, 10% hope.

name: Cyclops Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon warship—giant glowing eye judging you before it beams half the galaxy. Pixel flipbook of space’s angriest flashlight.

name: Devastator Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Cosmicon warship that trades subtlety for pure firepower. Frame by frame of a flying sledgehammer reminding fleets that shields are optional.

name: Auracore Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon station—spin-to-win buffs blasting fleets like cosmic Gatorade. Pixel fidget spinner that trades dizzy for deadly.

name: Spawnforge Spritesheet
description: Common Webe factory—space sweatshop spitting cannon fodder at light speed. Pixel flipbook of nightmares entering mass production.

name: Warp Portal Spritesheet
description: Common Webe warp ring—haunted hula hoop ripping rifts and vomiting fleets. Pixel proof that cosmic shortcuts are never safe.

name: Needler Spritesheet
description: Common Webe rifle-ship—long, mean, basically a gun with thrusters. Pixel frames screaming target practice while fleets get ventilated.

name: Hivebreaker Spritesheet
description: Common Webe warship—strategy skipped, headbutts eternal. Pixel flipbook of a cosmic battering ram auditioning for demolition derby.

name: Hornet Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Spirat pest-ship—small, fast, and always showing up in swarms. Frame by frame of the galaxy’s worst buzzing migraine.

name: Buran Spritesheet
description: Common Webe bruiser—whale-shaped, bird-cosplay bulk. Wide, heavy, and belly-flops through space while still flattening fleets.

name: Boomer Spritesheet
description: Common Webe kamikaze—slow, dumb, stuffed with explosives. Pixel cargo hauler that tricks you right up until it goes full boom-shakalaka.

name: MK-IV Ultra Spritesheet
description: Common Neutral prototype—fighter blazing with starlight cores, flexing like a lab experiment with ego. Pixel solar-flare overkill on repeat.

name: Stingray Spritesheet
description: Common Celestial strike ship—glides like a manta, then zaps hulls with storm juice. Pixel proof that elegance can still be an electric jerk.

name: Graviton Spritesheet
description: Common Webe gravity bruiser—slower than tax forms, hits like a black hole tantrum. Pixel frames of cosmic paperwork turning into pain.

name: Orion Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Cosmicon duck fighter—flaps like poultry, blasts like artillery. Frame by frame of plasma quacks turning fleets into cosmic breadcrumbs.

name: Olmec Spritesheet
description: Common Webe fortress—an angry cube-face spitting fire. Pixel by pixel proof that defense can double as a pissed-off monument.

name: Phantom Spritesheet
description: Common Celestial stealth ship—claims invisibility while glowing like a rave stick. Pixel by pixel, cosmic hide-and-seek with a neon sign.

name: Predator Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Cosmicon destroyer with the giant space-maw—basically a rave shark charging frame by frame, hungry for bandwidth and bad decisions.

name: Podcrasher Spritesheet
description: Common Webe kamikaze pod—pixel flipbook of a hive drone screaming 'YOLO' at light speed. No strategy, just slam and hope it explodes.

name: Ragnarok Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe warship that hums like a bad lightbulb but still wrecks fleets. Frame by frame of pure overcompensation in motion.

name: Nanocore Spritesheet
description: Common Webe mech-ship—tank frame, mech fists, hive fury. Pixel by pixel, it chews through fleets like overtime rage with metal payback.

name: Dinobot Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe brawler that charges like a space T-Rex with anger management issues. Frame by frame of a prehistoric headbutt clinic in zero-G.

name: Bulleteye Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon warship—sleek shark-dolphin hull with tail-fin swagger. Pixel by pixel, a cosmic sea beast blasting holes in fleets.

name: Warhawk Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon scorpion ship—pincers snapping, armor flexing. Pixel frames proving strategy’s dead when this thing charges through.

name: Forgeblock Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon cube factory—pumping out ships like a galactic vending machine. Pixel by pixel of disciplined industry in brick cosplay.

name: Lineforge Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Spirat ship factory—long, thin, and spitting out raiders like they’re on clearance sale. Every frame is just pirate capitalism done wrong.

name: Seer Spritesheet
description: Common Celestial scout—tiny, twitchy, more sensors than guns. Frame by frame of a glowing snitch moonlighting as a fortune-teller.

name: Xenopulse Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe strike craft—cheap, fast, and swarming like interstellar termites with tasers. Frame by frame of bad manners and worse shocks.

name: Cuda Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon bruiser—sleek, loud, zero finesse. Frame by frame of a space predator that skips tactics and goes straight for the bite.

name: Overdrive Spritesheet
description: Common Webe bruiser—flies like Superman late for comic-con, arms out, blasting through space in frame-by-frame hive hero cosplay.

name: Wargloom Spritesheet
description: Common Spirat warship—Ragnarok’s angrier, mass-produced twin. Frame by frame of pirate copy-paste hardware gone feral.

name: CR3 Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Webe killing machine—still no feelings, no mercy, no breaks. Just frame by frame of a hive murderbot running cosmic delete.exe on fleets.

name: Zenith Spritesheet
description: Common Cosmicon support—nanobots like cosmic glitter, warp beacon vibes. Frame by frame, it’s basically interstellar Uber with free band-aids.

name: Warhawk II
description: Epic Cosmicon Titan—scorpion ship overdosed on glow. Pincers snap, thrusters scream, the definition of 'extra' before it flattens you.

name: Warhawk III
description: Common Cosmicon Titan—scorpion ship in no-frills mode. Still cracks fleets apart, just skipped the nightclub lights and makeup.

name: Warhawk Trio
description: Three Cosmicon scorpion warships from different clans—basically a murder boyband where the only choreography is flattening fleets in sync.

name: Warhawk Squad
description: Common Cosmicon squad—five Warhawks in sun-faded pastels. Still crush fleets, just look more like knockoff toys than terror.

name: Warhawk IV
description: Common Cosmicon Titan—scorpion ship in front-view glory. Pincers out, lights blazing, like a cosmic recruitment poster nobody asked for.

name: Bulleteye
description: Cosmicon warship shaped like a fishbowl torpedo—short, stubby, and still dumb enough to ram fleets head-on. Pink glow makes it look friendly, until it isn’t.

name: John Sorrow
description: Legendary Spirat—once a proud Cosmicon, now a pity parade with guns. Cosmic trash turned tragic proof that betrayal hurts worse than plasma.

name: Soul of Aeon
description: 2016 Celestial pitch for an eternal guardian—canceled like a bad reboot, now lingering as a rare soul flexing immortality it never had.

name: Soul of Hannah
description: 2016 Cosmicon draft—hero pose with a dirtless drone, now haunting the archives like a space-only relic nobody needed.

name: Soul of Armadillo Soldier
description: 2016 Spirat concept—armadillo cosplay in full armor, visor down, forever rolling through the archives like a rejected mascot.

name: Soul of Armadillo Champion
description: 2016 Spirat concept—armored armadillo pointing skyward like it won. It didn’t. Retired pre-battle, now flexes eternal false glory.

name: Soul of Armadillo Elder
description: 2016 Spirat concept—armored to the teeth yet cane in hand. Half warrior, half nursing-home escapee, limping eternal as a Soul.

name: Soul of Plagnor
description: 2016 Spirat concept—frog soldier flexing in the uncanny valley between badass and meme. Later redesigned, but the cringe lives on.

name: Soul of Beacon
description: 2016 Celestial concept—a holy guide-ship that 3D botched into a cosmic oopsie. The model died, the Soul shines on with what-ifs.

name: Cosmicrafts Logo
description: 2018 relic—Cosmicrafts’ glowing-text era, when neon letters were meant to carry a galaxy. Brand baby steps into space chaos.

name: Soul of Ironhide
description: 2016 Spirat concept—armadillo Soul with a gun bigger than its family tree. Tank vibes in lizard cosplay, too badass to vanish.

name: Soul of Golem Assault
description: 2016 Webe concept—steampunk war machine of gears and steam that died in 3D. Looked brutal on paper, lives on as Soul-shaped disappointment.

name: Soul of Xulthorg Maw
description: 2016 Arch concept—antennae, mandibles, and nightmare fuel. Too creepy even for Webes, it never hit 3D, just lingers on as a Soul.

name: Soul of Anu'thar
description: Arch concept from 2016—scarab-bodied and built like it could bench-press a planet. Stronk as hell in sketches, never made it past concept limbo.

name: Soul of Ichorath
description: 2016 Arch concept—beetle warrior with a heavy carapace and heavier vibes. Never made it past sketch, now crawls on as a lingering Soul.

name: Soul of John Sorrow II
description: 2017 Spirat concept—fallen Cosmicon brooding with eyeliner angst. Betrayal never made it past sketch, but the Soul still lingers.

name: Soul of John Sorrow III
description: 2016 Spirat concept—John Sorrow as a confused intern sketch, half Cosmicon, half Spirat, all foreshadowing of the mess to come.

name: Soul of Plagnor II
description: 2016 Spirat concept—same rebel frog, but moodier, shadow-soaked, like the artist wanted him drowning in their bad dreams too.

name: Soul of Plagnor III
description: 2017 Spirat concept—rear view of Plagnor. Not turning his back, just frog-prophecy mode, staring into the future like it owes him rent.

name: Soul of John Hook
description: 2017 Spirat concept—hook hand, thrift-shop pirate coat, and the vibe of eyeliner + vengeance as a full personality build.

name: Soul of John Sorrow IV
description: 2017 Spirat concept—cyber-eye DLC, trench coat of secrets or bad fashion. Less pirate, more space outlaw LinkedIn profile pic.

name: Soul of John's Back
description: 2017 concept art of John Sorrow looking back, but it's not giving you the back, its looking towards the future...

name: Soul of Skarr Redfang
description: Armored alligator with a plasma rifle,, laser strapped, and looking like he’s ready to charge extra for swamp tours.

name: Soul of Warp Portal
description: Prototype gate frame that looked ready to open wormholes but got benched before hitting 3D production.

name: Soul of Octeslas
description: Early Webe prototype that looks like a jellyfish decided to cosplay as a motherboard.

name: Soul of Logo Prototype A
description: Rough star-cut logo concept—looked more like a stencil than a banner. Early draft that didn’t survive polish.

name: Soul of Logo Prototype B
description: Chunky star-G hybrid—looked like clipart with ambitions. Another early logo soul that got scrapped fast.

name: Soul of Tri-Faction Chaos
description: Spirats, Spades, and Webes all shoved into one piece—like a crossover episode nobody asked for but still turned out epic.

name: Soul of Siegebreaker
description: Cosmicon tank concept with twin cannons—basically a space bulldozer designed to erase fortresses.

name: Soul of Spade Miscast
description: Supposed to be a Spade, ended up looking like an underwater ballerina with antlers. Bad art direction, peak comedy.

name: Soul of Wheeled Drone
description: Cosmicon prototype that ditched flight for wheels—basically a tripod on training wheels.

name: Soul of Steamweaver A
description: Early Webe prototype with full steampunk goggles-and-gears energy—like a robot that moonlights as a train conductor.

name: Soul of Steamweaver B
description: Another Webe draft in steampunk drag—pipes, rivets, and enough brass fittings to start a jazz band.

name: Soul of Ygg'Ploth
description: Early Arch god sketch—rough as hell, but nails the vision of a cosmic world-eater straight out of nightmares.

name: Soul of Solar Paladin
description: 2017 concept of a cosmic knight rocking blazing hair inside a spacesuit—like if a lion decided to cosplay as a saint.

name: Soul of Beacon II
description: Webe concept channeling full Matrix squid energy—tentacles, wires, and one big staring eye.

name: Drillshot II
description: Legendary artwork of the Webe grunt ship Drillshot—two barrels, no mercy, painted like the hive’s poster child for overkill.

name: Jumper
description: Neutral station that powers up and shoves fleets back—basically the galaxy’s bouncer with an energy tab.

name: Emblem of Spades
description: The official badge of the Spades—fangs, eyes, and menace all packed into one hellish grin.

name: Emblem of Spirats
description: Updated Spirats badge after 2020—sharper, meaner, carrying that modern outlaw edge.

name: Mixed Wing Squad
description: A rare squad composition mixing multiple ship classes—less uniform fleet, more cosmic garage band of warships.

name: Wingflare Squad
description: A full Webe squad of Wingflares—five thruster-rave gnats screaming across the void in formation.

name: Warhawk Devastator Squad
description: A heavy Cosmicon formation—one Warhawk at the core, flanked by Devastators like wingmen with way too much firepower.

name: Dominator Squad II
description: Cosmicon Dominators rolling deep—heavy bruisers in formation, lighting up space like flying siege towers.

name: Stargate
description: Cosmicon station that tears open the void—massive ring of light that spits fleets across the galaxy like an interstellar slingshot.

name: Steampunk blueprint
description: 2016 draft that looks more blueprint than battleship—gears, valves, and a robot face straight out of a Victorian fever dream.

name: Xenopulse II
description: Webe fighter pulsing toxic green—basically a space bug zapper that forgot which side it’s on.

name: Xenopulse III
description: Rare Webe fighter variant—same bug-eyed menace, now with a glowing aura that screams 'premium pest control.'

name: Overdrive
description: Bottom view of the Webe bruiser—still blasting forward like Superman, but now you just get the thruster glow and a hive butt pose.

name: The Terraformer II
description: Cosmicon base that reshapes worlds to Wegnar’s will—half citadel, half planet-sized garden tool.

name: Tigershark II
description: Rear view of the Cosmicon strike ship—violet cores blazing, engines flaring like it’s showing off its afterburner tattoos.

name: Tigershark III
description: Cosmicon strike ship tearing through space with twin beams—fast, sharp, and loud enough to make fleets flinch.

name: Packet Hub
description: Looks like a floating server rack with antennas—basically the Webes’ idea of Wi-Fi coverage in deep space.

name: Data Spire
description: Tall, boxy, and full of blinking lights—basically a galactic router that probably crashes when too many fleets connect.

name: Kernel Bastion
description: Square-bodied and stubborn, a defensive node with all the charm of a firewall that bans everyone equally.

name: Signal Forge
description: An ugly little cube that screams strength in numbers—built to churn out signals like cosmic spam mail.

name: Cache Node
description: Half warehouse, half hard drive—a Webe outpost that hoards packets like dragons hoard gold.

name: Grid Vault
description: Boxy station with sharp edges and way too many antennas—pretty much a cosmic IT department nobody asked for.

name: Protocol Keep
description: Looks like a floating government building, but it’s really just Webes making sure everyone follows their ridiculous packet rules.

name: Logic Outpost
description: Symmetrical to a fault—this is what happens when Webes let an algorithm design architecture. Efficient, soulless, and ready to crash.

name: Sentry
description: Webe station that’s basically a floating gun rack—three barrels of pure ‘shut up and die’ energy, mounted on a cube that doesn’t even pretend to look fancy.

name: Torretuda
description: Cosmicon strike craft that took the Barracuda frame and bolted turrets on top—because subtlety is overrated when you can be a flying battleship in miniature.

name: Assembler Line
description: Webe station that looks more like a factory bolted together in zero-g—modules linked up like it’s cranking out hive tech straight off the conveyor belt.

name: CR3-Terminator II
description: Legendary Webe warship, a flying execution script with wings—turns battlefields into error logs with relentless precision.

name: Gemini II
description: Rare Celestial specialist—twin-core vessel fighting like two souls in one hull, turning skirmishes into radiant duets of ruin.

name: Emblem of Pending
description: Neutral badge of eternal buffering—glows forever, mocks your patience, and reminds the galaxy that some confirmations never come.

name: Doom II
description: Cosmicon titan—hulking slab of annihilation with firepower to make stars nervous. Its silhouette alone screams game over.

name: Doom III
description: Rare Cosmicon titan—neon fortress humming with menace, its every thruster burn and cannon blast a prophecy of annihilation.

name: XRT Overseer
description: Rare Cosmicon turret-station—exposes cloaked ships, pins them with beams, and fries systems mid-slink. Hide-and-seek ends in fire.

name: XRT Oblivion
description: Epic Cosmicon turret-station that shreds stealth fleets with ion lightning—turning would-be sneaks into cosmic confetti.

name: Brainleech II
description: Rare Celestial support—cosmic parasite draining shields and scrambling systems. Space barnacle vibes, with bonus Wi-Fi theft.

name: Brainleech III
description: Common Celestial support—clings to hulls and drains power like a glowing space tick. Harmless solo, nightmare when the swarm arrives.

name: Barracuda
description: Cosmicon specialist with thrusters so oversized they scream overcompensation—plows through fleets with blunt, fuel-soaked intimidation.

name: Barracuda II
description: Epic Cosmicon specialist—slices blockades like a buzzsaw, thrusters blazing arcs that prove subtlety was kicked out the airlock.

name: Humpback
description: Webe support ship—fortress hull scarred in neon, waddling like a space hump while hauling shields and drones to keep fleets alive.

name: Crab III
description: Rare Cosmicon interceptor—battle-scarred shell and crackling pincers turn this once comic crawler into a scuttling cosmic nightmare.

name: Ironfoundry
description: Webe factory-station, a scrapyard on steroids—welding, bolting, and spitting out ships in paranoid overdrive before fleets can blink.

name: Neon Scaffold
description: Webe construction-station that’s half shipyard, half hazard zone—rage-quit city planning held together with duct tape and code.

name: Circuit Pile
description: Webe spacestation of server racks, vending machines, and chaos—basically production-ready code spaghetti that somehow powers fleets.

name: Cyclops II
description: Cosmicon warship with a single glaring pink core—an eye that burns brighter than shame. Its beams cut through fleets like a rave gone wrong.

name: Cyclops III
description: Cosmicon warship powered by a cold blue core—its eye doesn’t blink, doesn’t flinch, just tracks you across light-years and burns clean through hulls.

name: Cyclops IV
description: Cosmicon warship with a venomous green eye-core—staring like a toxic god. It vomits beams that corrode shields and pride at the same time.

name: Tri-Cyclops
description: Three Cosmicon Cyclops in formation—triple eyes, triple beams. A galactic traffic stop where the fine is instant vaporization.

name: Devastator
description: Frontline bruiser with dual plasma cannons that light up like stadium lamps before tearing ships in half. The Devastator doesn’t aim—it declares.

name: Devastator II
description: Cosmicon destroyer glowing with violet overcharge—a cannon-stuffed bunker that turns ambushes into purple firework shows.

name: Devastator III
description: Rare Cosmicon destroyer—just a blurred silhouette with thrusters blazing. If you spot it, the fight’s already over.

name: Devastator IV
description: Cosmicon destroyer clad in jagged armor and thruster fins—a fortress with engines, looming heavy enough to rewrite battle plans.

name: Devastator V
description: Green-lit and savage, this Devastator prowls like a predator with headlights. Fast, loud, and merciless—it doesn’t fight fair, it fights final.

name: Devastator VI
description: Cosmicon destroyer with regal armor and cobalt exhaust—doesn’t just fight, it arrives like royalty and leaves carnage as confetti.

name: Dominator IV
description: Cosmicon support ship wrapped in violet arcs—less healer, more stormcloud. Its aura alone makes foes feel trial by execution.

name: Orion IV
description: Cosmicon fighter blazing with golden thrusters—cuts through the void like a shooting star, but up close it’s more firework than fortress.

name: Buran
description: Webe titan that drifts like a caffeinated space whale—armored, over-engined, and graceful as a meteor crash, but brutally effective.

name: Phantom
description: Celestial specialist—half warship, half space sorcerer—slips past sensors in neon robes, glowing like a ghost across the stars.

name: Podcrasher IV
description: Webe interceptor built for demolition derbies—oversized thrusters, zero self-preservation, pure flying middle finger energy.

name: Nanocore (Blue-Core)
description: Webe destroyer variant glowing with an icy blue core—cold, unyielding, and built to freeze fleets in awe before tearing them apart.

name: Nanocore
description: A rare Webe destroyer variant bristling with twin gatling arrays—less spaceship, more industrial shredder with thrusters strapped on.

name: Nanocore OG
description: A Webe destroyer running on a pulsating magenta core—firing salvos like a neon rave cannon, lighting up space battles with brutal elegance.

name: Nanocore (Green-Core)
description: Webe destroyer variant fueled by a blazing green core—burns through targets with industrial fury, like a foundry turned warship.

name: Dinobot III
description: Webe destroyer that headbutts like a neon dino nightmare—fast, heavy, and savage enough to turn battles into lightshows.

name: Soul of Orbital Fortress
description: Neutral baseline fortress—no frills, just a hulking orbital hub holding fleets together with factory-like discipline.

name: Dinobot Spritesheet 2
description: Spritesheet of the Webe brawler that charges like a space T-Rex with anger management issues. Frame by frame of a prehistoric headbutt clinic in zero-G.

name: Wraith Spritesheet
description: Spritesheet of the Cosmicon heavy fighter—carries more firepower than its frame should, basically a flying arsenal with wings that scream ‘overcompensation.’

name: Xenopulse IV
description: Backview of the Webe strike craft with crimson glow—flies like it’s daring you to shoot it, then fries you faster than you can blink.

name: Xenopulse V
description: Webe strike craft crackling with neon fury—built like a space dagger, lunges forward in swarms and carves holes through enemy lines.

name: Xenopulse Variant C
description: Webe strike craft pulsing with green-core energy—flies erratic like a hornet on overdrive, stings harder the closer it swarms.
